english.title: Racially aggravated harassment - non violent
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) pursued a course of conduct which amounted to the harassment of **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) and which you knew or ought to have known amounted to the harassment of

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_

in that **(..DETAIL DATES, PLACES AND NATURE OF CONDUCT..) which was racially aggravated in accordance with section 28 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998
english.legislation: Contrary to section 32(1)(a) of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
pursued a course of conduct which amounted to harassment
which you knew/ought to have known amounted to harassment
the offence was racially aggravated OR
being aware that such conduct was likely to have that effect

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
This CJS Code and Standard Offence Wording is OBSOLETE. Now see CJS Code CD98069 and Offence Wording H10006.

(i) The option to return an alternative verdict of guilty of the basic offence is NOT available in the magistrates court, therefore the basic offence should be charged in addition to the aggravated offence.
(ii) See offence wording H5 for note re: conduct required pursuant to section 7 of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997.
(iii) If, on trial on indictments of a person charged with this offence, the jury find him not guilty of the offence charged, they may find him guilty of the basic offence in section 2 of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997.
(iv) For the religiously or religiously/racially wordings see offence wordings H4742 and H4743.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
